baseline.methodology: Synchronous lexer + SourceDocument/line index + parser/normal lowerings per identical source sequence. JIT warmed; 31 batches; per-sequence latency/allocation divided by repetitions. No resolver, checker, I/O or cursor repair. Full public AST property graph fingerprint (tokens, type nodes, values and flags) computed outside timing, with no fields excluded. Retained heap is noisy full-GC live delta with final documents and AST roots alive; index estimate excludes base text/tokens/AST. Baseline archived without source instrumentation.

investigation: Ordinary parsing stays below the 10% investigation threshold on both fixtures; allocations increase about 0.31%.
Enabled capture has a measured 4.58x/4.93x parse-pipeline latency and 2.45x/2.44x allocations relative to current ordinary parsing; absolute additional latency is 0.19024ms/7.6632ms.

Code inspection attributes enabled-only work to provenance collection/deduplication, final AST/type/attachment reachability, span pruning, immutable array copies/sorts and frozen reference-keyed node indexes. This is attribution by inspection, not measured phase profiling.
Extra allocated bytes per syntax record remain approximately constant across the fixtures (763B/761B), consistent with bounded linear data growth rather than a new allocation scaling problem.

Retained heap covers complete final documents and AST roots; the editor index estimate covers index structures only. Full-GC heap deltas are noisy. Editor metadata is captured on a cold parse and reused by checked snapshots; end-to-end interactive budgets will be evaluated by #1981.
